questions.explanation: Sperm cells are produced in the testes (singular: testis) by meiosis. The testes are located in the scrotum outside the body, which maintains them at a slightly lower temperature than body temperature, optimal for sperm production.

questions.stem: What is the function of the vas deferens?

options.text: To carry sperm from the testes to the urethra

questions.explanation: The vas deferens (sperm duct) is a muscular tube that carries sperm from the epididymis (where sperm are stored and mature) to the urethra during ejaculation.

questions.stem: What do the prostate gland and seminal vesicles produce?

options.text: Fluids that nourish and protect sperm (seminal fluid)

questions.explanation: The prostate gland and seminal vesicles produce seminal fluid, which combines with sperm to form semen. This fluid provides nutrients (such as fructose) and an alkaline environment to protect and nourish the sperm.

questions.stem: Which hormone controls the development of male secondary sexual characteristics?
questions.explanation: Testosterone is produced by the testes and controls the development of male secondary sexual characteristics during puberty, including deepening of the voice, growth of facial and body hair, and increased muscle mass.

questions.stem: Why are the testes located outside the body in the scrotum?

options.text: To keep them at a slightly lower temperature than body temperature for sperm production
To allow easier connection to the urethra
To make testosterone production more efficient

questions.explanation: Sperm production requires a temperature slightly lower than normal body temperature (about 35 degrees C rather than 37 degrees C). The scrotum holds the testes outside the body cavity to maintain this cooler temperature.

questions.stem: How are sperm cells adapted for their function?

options.text: They have a thick cell wall for protection
They have a large food store and no nucleus
They have a tail for swimming, many mitochondria for energy, and an acrosome with enzymes
They are very large cells to carry more genetic material

questions.explanation: Sperm cells have a streamlined head, a tail (flagellum) for swimming to the egg, many mitochondria in the middle section to provide energy for movement, and an acrosome containing enzymes to penetrate the egg.

questions.stem: What is the tube shared by both the urinary and reproductive systems in males?
questions.explanation: The urethra is the tube that runs through the penis and carries both urine (from the bladder) and semen (during ejaculation). A valve ensures that both cannot pass through at the same time.
